data.content_ref: inline:SRC_03's 'theory-quality × execution-fidelity' framework is incomplete because it omits aggregation as an independent reliability factor. Its third countercondition admits Condorcet-style aggregation can provide a reliability boost independent of the frozen theory's quality. Yet the main claim asserts the panel outperforms the expert ONLY if the frozen theory's quality exceeds the expert's internal theory. This ignores the orthogonal benefit of independent-error cancellation, which can yield superior reliability even when checklist quality is lower than the expert's theory.
